entries.name_han: 大洞玉经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that liberation is not gained by external petition alone but by interiorly uniting the bodily pantheon with the Great Cavern (大洞) hierarchy through recitation-visualization. Mortality persists while the microcosmic gods remain scattered; when the thirty-nine (or parallel jade) stanzas reassemble them into one luminous axis, the practitioner becomes co-extensive with the highest Shangqing reality and can exit the cycle of form.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the human body already contains true gods homologous to celestial offices. 2) Premise: ordinary mind disperses these gods, so destiny remains locked in decay. 3) Inference: only scriptural sound plus ordered visualization can call each deity back to its seat. 4) Inference: their simultaneous presence opens the Great Cavern passageway. 5) Conclusion: the self is no longer a private organism but a node of the Shangqing hierarchy, hence capable of ascent and long life.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map natal chart deities (命宫、身宫、主星) as interior officers analogous to Shangqing body-gods. 2) Recite or silently hold a short Dadong-style hymn while visualizing each officer returning to its palace. 3) Use day-master strength as a proxy for whether the 'axis' is assembled or scattered. 4) Prefer cultivation hours that match the chart's strongest elemental season to reinforce reunion. 5) Treat repeated BaZi 'empty' or 'clash' years as periods when body-gods are dislodged and require re-stabilizing ritual.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Lingbao salvation scriptures that emphasize universal deliverance through liturgy for others, this text argues for elite interior theurgy of the self. Unlike Zhengyi covenant texts that locate authority in received registers, it locates authority in the successful reassembly of innate body-gods. The difference follows from Shangqing’s claim that the highest path is contemplative identity with the Cavern, not bureaucratic petition or communal mass salvation.

entries.name_han: 太上老君说上七元真人金轩玉字经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that destiny is administratively held by the Upper Seven Yuan Perfected of the Dipper, and that 'jade characters' plus golden-carriage symbolism are the lawful tokens by which a mortal may be enrolled under their protection. Random piety does not move the Seven Yuan; only alignment with their script-and-title system reclassifies the person from unprotected commoner to guarded subordinate of the northern astral court.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: lifespan, calamity, and rank are filed under the Seven Yuan of the Dipper. 2) Premise: the Seven Yuan respond to correct names, titles, and jade-character seals, not to private emotion alone. 3) Inference: receiving or reciting the golden-carriage jade script places the devotee on their register. 4) Inference: once registered, adverse astral influences must pass their checkpoint. 5) Conclusion: protection and advancement are bureaucratic effects of correct celestial enrollment, not mere luck.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, treat the seven Dipper correspondences and the northern water/metal axis as the chart’s 'Seven Yuan file.' 2) When 七杀、羊刃、空亡 threaten life or status, petition or meditate specifically to the relevant Yuan rather than a generic deity. 3) Use name-rectification and seal/talisman logic (correct '玉字') before major year transitions. 4) Schedule Dipper rites on 庚申、甲子 or the native’s 本命 day to re-file the chart. 5) Read sudden rank or travel luck as '金轩' response after enrollment, not random fortune.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with the broader Beidou/Wudou life-extension suite, this scripture narrows agency to the Upper Seven Yuan and their jade-character protocol. Unlike pure moral 感应 texts, it insists on scriptural-talismanic credentials. The difference matters because it treats salvation as astral bureaucracy with seals, not only as virtue-response or generic star worship.

entries.name_han: 灵宝自然经诀
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that efficacious Lingbao method is valid only when it conforms to cosmic spontaneity (自然): rites, breaths, and texts work because they express the Dao’s self-so order, not because the operator forces results. Forced technique without natural correspondence breeds disorder; method that rides the pre-existing grain of Heaven-Earth becomes self-authenticating power.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Dao’s primary mode is ziran—uncontrived self-emergence. 2) Premise: human artifice that fights this grain creates friction and false spirits. 3) Inference: true Lingbao formulae are 'natural keys' that unlock what already wants to open. 4) Inference: verification is ease, resonance, and non-straining effect, not theatrical force. 5) Conclusion: cultivation and ritual succeed by consenting to cosmic grain, not by conquering it.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In chart reading, prefer remedies that follow the chart’s strongest seasonal flow (顺势) over brutal counter-elements. 2) Time talisman or meditation work to open stems/branches rather than fighting closed clocks. 3) If a practice produces strain, re-diagnose misalignment with ziran instead of increasing force. 4) Use fasting, breath, and text as soft keys that clear channels, not as weapons. 5) Evaluate BaZi 'useful god' strategy by whether life becomes simpler and more coherent after adoption.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike thunder-method scriptures that authorize violent rectification of demons, this text privileges non-forcing naturalness. Unlike Shangqing’s dense interior pantheon maps, it emphasizes methodological congruence with spontaneity over deity inventory. The difference encodes Lingbao’s claim that the highest technique is non-technique aligned with cosmic self-so.

entries.name_han: 太上三五正一盟威修真玉经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that authentic cultivation (修真) under the Zhengyi lineage is inseparable from the Three-Five covenant of authority (三五正一盟威): spiritual power is a licensed office conferred by celestial contract, not a private talent. Without the covenant, techniques are unauthorized and may be prosecuted by the same spirit courts they attempt to command; with it, the adept becomes a lawful deputy of the One.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the spirit world is a government requiring seals, oaths, and ranks. 2) Premise: the Zhengyi covenant is the classical charter empowering mortals to act within that government. 3) Inference: 'Three-Five' methods are operative only as functions of that charter. 4) Inference: self-made magic without alliance is both weak and culpable. 5) Conclusion: refining the true self means accepting official appointment under the Dao’s law, then practicing within its limits.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat lineage transmission, precepts, and registers as non-optional 'legal standing' for ritual BaZi remedies. 2) Before commanding spirits of years/months, check whether the operator has ethical and covenantal right. 3) Use 正 (orthodoxy) as a diagnostic: chaotic results often mean unauthorized method. 4) Frame chart rectification as filing a lawful petition, not as hacking fate. 5) In cultivation, pair technical practice with vow, purity rules, and accountability to a master-system.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Dadong’s interior ascent without primary appeal to Celestial Master registers, this text centers bureaucratic license. Unlike purely philosophical Laozi exegeses, it makes law and oath the condition of power. The difference is Zhengyi’s foundational thesis: efficacy without covenant is counterfeit.

entries.name_han: 太上紫微玄都雷霆玉经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that thunder (雷霆) is not raw weather but the executive arm of the Purple Tenuity–Mysterious Capital court, deployed to punish disorder and restore cosmic statute. Calling thunder is therefore a judicial act: it is justified when aligned with Ziwei Xuandu’s mandate and unjust when used as private violence. The scripture legitimates thunder rites as celestial law enforcement.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: highest stellar sovereignty (紫微) and capital of mystery (玄都) oversee order. 2) Premise: thunder departments are their punitive and purifying instruments. 3) Inference: demons, epidemics, and social chaos are legal breaches, not mere accidents. 4) Inference: correct jade-script/thunder protocol activates lawful force. 5) Conclusion: rectification by thunder succeeds only as delegated justice under the northern court.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read severe 七杀、羊刃、刑冲 combinations as 'cases' that may need thunder-style clearing, not only soft nourishment. 2) Invoke thunder logic only after moral self-audit—never as aggression for private gain. 3) Time such work on days of strong fire-metal movement or storm-season qi. 4) Pair with confession and restitution so the 'court' sees a clean docket. 5) In BaZi counseling, treat sudden calamity as possible enforcement, then seek lawful pacification.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Three Officials texts that stress confession and calendrical pardon, this text stresses force as justice. Unlike pure 感应 moral tracts, it supplies a military-judicial hierarchy of thunder. The difference is Song–Yuan leifa’s claim that the cosmos polices itself through thunder bureaucracy centered on Ziwei.

entries.name_han: 玄天上帝感应经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Xuantian Shangdi (Zhenwu) responds (感应) in strict proportion to the devotee’s sincerity, purity, and moral alignment with northern true-martial order. The god is not a vending machine of favors; resonance is a two-pole circuit—human uprightness completes the circuit, hypocrisy opens a short that yields no protection or even reverse reckoning.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Zhenwu embodies true north, martial rectitude, and demon-subduing clarity. 2) Premise: ganying requires matching frequency between human heart and divine virtue. 3) Inference: ritual without inner truth fails to couple the circuit. 4) Inference: consistent virtue plus focused devotion produces protective response. 5) Conclusion: disasters recede and fortunes stabilize when the person becomes a resonant image of the Dark Heaven’s order.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For charts overloaded with yin-water, hidden bloodshed, or chaotic 杀, use Zhenwu as the rectifying archetype. 2) Precede petition with concrete ethical correction (debts, speech, lust, violence). 3) Practice northern orientation, stillness, and martial discipline of mind as the 'antenna.' 4) Track response as improved timing and fewer self-inflicted clashes, not only omens. 5) On 庚、壬 days or 玄天 festivals, renew the vow of non-harm and clarity.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike City God or Stove King scriptures focused on local domestic/territorial mediation, this centers a high martial cosmic sovereign. Unlike talisman-only life-extension texts, it makes moral resonance the primary switch. The difference is Zhenwu cult logic: northern true-martial virtue is the key, not kitchen ethics or municipal bureaucracy alone.

entries.name_han: 太上说三官大帝本行经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Heaven, Earth, and Water Officials form a complete tripartite court that records, judges, and remits human deeds across all domains of life. Because every action falls under at least one Official, confession and petition to the Three Officials can rebalance karmic accounts that no single-star or single-local deity fully covers. The '本行' narrative legitimates their jurisdiction by origin story.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: moral and destinic consequences are filed in three realms—sky, land, waters. 2) Premise: the Three Officials are the instituted judges of those realms. 3) Inference: guilt and merit are not private feelings but archival facts in their offices. 4) Inference: on triune assembly days, lawful confession can amend the archive. 5) Conclusion: calamity and blessing track the state of one’s Three Officials dossier.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map BaZi disasters to realms: career/authority→天官, property/body/home→地官, emotion/sex/travel/flow→水官. 2) Use 三元 days for confession protocols tied to the matching official. 3) Before major luck-cycle changes, clear the dossier rather than only boosting wealth gods. 4) Design remedies that include restitution in the same realm as the offense. 5) Read repeated water or earth penalties as unclosed 水官/地官 cases.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Dongyue’s underworld-life/death focus or City God’s municipal scope, the Three Officials claim pan-domain coverage. Unlike pure star-dipper life texts, they emphasize moral archive over astral calculation alone. The difference is structural: triune jurisdiction as the master ledger of Chinese religious destiny.

entries.name_han: 太上妙始经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that all later forms, names, and fortunes are secondary crystallizations of a marvelous primordial beginning (妙始), and that recovery of health, clarity, and immortality requires reverse-engineering existence back to that subtle origin. Working only at the level of symptoms and branch phenomena leaves the root unaddressed; contacting the pre-differentiated source rewrites the whole tree.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the cosmos unfolds from a subtle, marvelous beginning prior to coarse names. 2) Premise: sickness, error, and fate-knots are late-stage differentiations. 3) Inference: techniques stuck at the late stage can only rearrange symptoms. 4) Inference: meditation and scripture that re-enter 妙始 access the generative root. 5) Conclusion: true repair is return to origin, not endless patching of effects.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, distinguish root (日主、月令、格局) from surface (transient gods, annual noise). 2) Cultivate pre-dawn stillness to taste qi before naming it as five phases. 3) When chart conflicts multiply, stop stacking talismans; return to breath and origin-mind. 4) Prefer one deep correction of useful-god strategy over many cosmetic fixes. 5) Use cosmogonic contemplation when the native’s life feels 'over-determined' by labels.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Benji jing’s philosophically articulated 'ultimate boundary' discourse often in dialogue with Buddhist emptiness, 妙始经 stays closer to Daoist cosmogonic return rhetoric. Unlike practical star-and-talisman scriptures, it offers almost no bureaucratic detail. The difference is priority: origin metaphysics first, application second.

entries.name_han: 太上说中斗大魁保命妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the Middle Dipper and its Great Kui officer specifically administer the conservation of life-mandate (保命), complementing other Dipper offices that govern rank, longevity petitions, or calamity in different ways. When life-force is leaking—illness, shock, short-span indicators—the correct court to address is Zhongdou, not a generic 'star god.' The scripture re-centers destiny work on the middle axis of the Dipper bureaucracy.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Dipper administration is internally specialized. 2) Premise: Middle Dipper/Great Kui holds the portfolio of protecting allotted life. 3) Inference: threats to ming (命) must be filed with that office. 4) Inference: offering, confession, and recitation on proper days reopen protective coverage. 5) Conclusion: stabilized life-mandate is a targeted bureaucratic outcome of Zhongdou alignment.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Flag BaZi patterns of weak day-master, heavy depletion, 空亡 on life palaces as 保命 cases. 2) On 本命 day or middle-month nodes, perform Zhongdou-oriented quiet rite. 3) Combine medical and lifestyle conservation with the petition—bureaucracy plus biology. 4) Avoid exhausting the body during years when life stars are clashed. 5) Use the 'middle' metaphor: rebalance extremes in the chart rather than only boosting ends.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Southern Dipper longevity or Northern Dipper destiny texts, this isolates the Middle Dipper’s protect-life function. Unlike 益筭 talisman scriptures that seek to increase the numerical tally, it emphasizes conservation and shielding of what is already allotted. The difference is portfolio specificity within the same Dipper government.

entries.name_han: 太上老君说益筭神符妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that celestial lifespan is a countable archive (筭) that can be increased when Laozi’s divine talismans are correctly applied against the real causes of premature death—demonic infestation, guilt, and disordered qi—not by wish alone. The talisman is a legal instrument that amends the numerical file after the path of harm is cut; without cutting harm, the seal has nothing to attach to.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: years of life are accounted as 筭 in celestial books. 2) Premise: disease, curse, and sin illegally or prematurely deduct from that account. 3) Inference: exorcistic and protective talismans stop unlawful deductions. 4) Inference: once leakage stops, authorized 益筭 seals can petition addition or restoration. 5) Conclusion: lengthened life is archival amendment after causal purification, mediated by Laozi’s talismanic law.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Translate short-span BaZi signatures into 'leaks' (blood, drugs, risk, chronic drain) and stop them first. 2) Use talisman/recitation phases: clear → protect → request increase. 3) Time work to the native’s 建禄/长生 directions rather than dead seasons. 4) Pair with confession so the archive sees merit, not only craft. 5) Reassess yearly 筭 pressure at birthdays and major luck changes.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Zhongdou 保命, which conserves mandate, this text explicitly aims to increase the count. Unlike pure moral ganying texts, it centers 神符 as the operative technology. The difference is quantitative archival engineering of lifespan under Laozi’s seal authority.

entries.name_han: 太上老君说七十二灶王经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that household destiny is continuously surveilled and reported through a differentiated stove-king system (七十二灶王), making the kitchen the cosmic interface of domestic morality and fortune. Because food, fire, and family conduct pass this node daily, neglect of stove ethics silently rewrites the household’s file in Heaven; reverence and purity rewrite it toward blessing.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the stove is not merely a hearth but an official reporting post. 2) Premise: multiple stove kings cover specialized domestic jurisdictions. 3) Inference: daily kitchen conduct generates constant data for celestial assessment. 4) Inference: pollution, waste, quarrels, and sacrilege at the stove corrupt the report. 5) Conclusion: household luck tracks stove order more tightly than occasional temple visits.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For family BaZi clusters, diagnose shared kitchen/fire dynamics as a single field. 2) Clean, orient, and ritually respect the cooking space as fate infrastructure. 3) Link digestive, financial, and quarrel patterns to stove disorder. 4) On stove-god festival cycles, reconcile family grievances and renew vows. 5) Teach clients that 'wealth god' work fails if the domestic fire report is dirty.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike City God scriptures (municipal public order) or Dongyue (death-life judiciary), this is intimate domestic bureaucracy. Unlike high Dipper life texts, it locates destiny in daily fire and food practice. The difference is scale: micro-household reporting as the base layer of cosmic credit.

entries.name_han: 太上老君说城隍感应消灾集福妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the City God is the lawful local mediator who can dissolve disaster and gather fortune for residents because territorial spirits hold intermediate jurisdiction between households and high heaven. Personal virtue still matters, but without territorial clearance, high petitions can be blocked at the municipal spirit gate; with City God resonance, local obstacles convert into protected blessing.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: every city/locale has a Chenghuang office overseeing living and dead within its walls. 2) Premise: many disasters are local-administrative (plague, injustice, unrest, haunted disputes). 3) Inference: such cases must be addressed to the territorial court first. 4) Inference: ganying with Chenghuang unblocks the local channel of blessing. 5) Conclusion: disaster relief and fortune-gathering are often municipal spirit politics, not only personal star work.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When a chart’s problems are neighborhood, lawsuit, epidemic, or property-bound, include City God petition. 2) Align offerings with the client’s actual residence jurisdiction. 3) Combine with civic ethics—no fraud, no land-harm—so the local court has grounds to help. 4) Use after moves, shop openings, or haunted real-estate issues. 5) Read sudden local protection as Chenghuang response, then maintain the relationship.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Stove King domestic focus, Chenghuang is public-territorial. Unlike Three Officials’ cosmic triune ledger, it is geographically bounded. The difference is Daoist political theology of place: fortune has a zip code, and the City God is its clerk.

entries.name_han: 太上说东岳大帝护国保民妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the Eastern Peak Emperor’s judicial sovereignty over life, death, and underworld registers is the structural reason he can protect both the state and the people. National safety and popular welfare are not separate from the soul-archive of Mount Tai’s court; when that court is honored and justice is not mocked, protective cover extends from empire to household.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Dongyue administers the books of life and death and judges souls. 2) Premise: a people and a state are aggregates of those registered lives. 3) Inference: disorder in the Peak’s justice manifests as public calamity. 4) Inference: scripture, rite, and moral governance realign the living with that court. 5) Conclusion: 护国保民 is the macro-effect of correct relation to the Eastern Peak judiciary.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat severe life-death indicators, ancestral debt, and epidemic years as Dongyue-docket issues. 2) For leaders or public roles in the chart, add national-people protection vows. 3) Use Eastern Peak pilgrimage/rite logic when underworld dreams or inheritance curses dominate. 4) Pair personal longevity work with justice practice (no wrongful harm). 5) In family lineage BaZi, clear ancestral cases before expecting descendant peace.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike City God (city-scale) and Stove King (home-scale), Dongyue is peak-scale judiciary of death and rebirth. Unlike thunder texts that emphasize immediate punitive force, it emphasizes archival judgment and protection through correct standing. The difference is Mount Tai’s unique role as master registry of mortality for realm and person.

entries.name_han: 仙苑编珠
entries.logic_thesis: It proves by curated hagiographic 'pearls' that immortality is a recurrent, pattern-bearing human outcome, not a mythic singularity: each condensed biography functions as an empirical token that certain virtues, methods, and encounters reliably open the immortal path. The anthology’s logic is inductive—many verified cases establish a practical genus of transcendence.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: isolated miracle stories can be dismissed as legend. 2) Premise: a carefully edited garden of many cases reveals repeating causal structures. 3) Inference: those structures (master encounter, purity, perseverance, specific arts) are transferable. 4) Inference: the reader should imitate the causal core, not the costume of each tale. 5) Conclusion: immortality is historically attested as a learnable pattern-space.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Extract from any immortal story the operable causes (timing, ethics, method), ignore ornament. 2) Match those causes to the native’s BaZi strengths (e.g., strong resource → study path; strong output → ritual/art path). 3) Build a personal 'pearl list' of three exemplars whose charts-of-life resemble the client’s constraints. 4) Use failures in hagiography as negative controls (what broke the path). 5) Review monthly whether practice still tracks a proven pattern or has drifted into fantasy.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 玄品录, which ranks worthies by mysterious grade, 仙苑编珠 emphasizes jewel-like condensation of exemplary episodes. Unlike doctrinal scriptures that argue from cosmology, it argues from case collection. The difference is method of proof: inductive hagiographic anthology versus hierarchical catalog or metaphysical thesis.

entries.name_han: 玄品录
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Daoist attainment is legible as ranked 'mysterious grades' (玄品): biographies are not equal anecdotes but ordered evidence of hierarchical realization. By placing persons on a scale of mystery, the text asserts that the Dao manifests in degrees, and that later aspirants should orient to the grade-structure rather than flatten all saints into one vague holiness.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: mysterious accomplishment varies in depth and office. 2) Premise: historical lives can be sorted into grades without denying their value. 3) Inference: ranking teaches discrimination between stages and types of attainment. 4) Inference: model selection should match one’s current grade-potential. 5) Conclusion: cultivation is ascent through intelligible ranks of the mysterious, documented in lives.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Diagnose a chart’s cultivation ceiling and gate (pattern, useful god, mentor stars) as a 'grade hypothesis.' 2) Choose practices appropriate to stage—ethics and breath before thunder command. 3) Use lineage biographies as a ladder, not a random inspiration feed. 4) Avoid spiritual inflation: if life evidence is grade-1, do not claim grade-9 methods. 5) Re-grade yearly based on verified capacity, not self-image.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 仙苑编珠’s pearl-anthology inductive style, 玄品录 is explicitly hierarchical and catalogic. Unlike cosmogonic or talisman sutras, its proof medium is ranked prosopography. The difference is pedagogical: it trains discernment of levels in the mysterious path.

entries.name_han: 太上升玄消灾护命妙经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that disasters are dissolved and life guarded when consciousness 'ascends the mysterious' (升玄)—rising from coarse panic and karmic entanglement into the clear, empty-mysterious register where afflictions lose their grip. Recitation is the elevator: sound and meaning lift the mind, and the lifted mind no longer co-produces the disaster field, so protection appears as a natural side-effect.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: calamity binds most tightly when mind is sunk in fear and turbidity. 2) Premise: the mysterious is a higher, clearer ontological register. 3) Inference: scriptural ascent relocates awareness into that register. 4) Inference: relocated awareness stops feeding the disaster’s causal loop. 5) Conclusion: 消灾护命 is achieved by elevation of state, not only by bargaining with lower spirits.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In acute BaZi disaster years, prioritize daily short recitation that elevates mood-qi before complex rites. 2) Pair with sleep, silence, and reduced conflict to keep the 'ascent' stable. 3) When chart shows heavy 劫煞、亡神, train non-reactivity as technical 护命. 4) Use morning practice to ascend before the day’s branches pull mind down. 5) Measure success as fewer self-amplifying crises, not only lucky omens.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike thunder or City God texts that outsource force to external offices, this centers ascent of mind as primary technology. Unlike long doctrinal treatises (本际、微旨), it is short, performative, and popular. The difference is emergency soteriology: elevate state quickly to cut disaster co-creation.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝圆明大义经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the 'great meaning' of Lingbao is round, complete luminosity (圆明): salvation and wisdom are the same event of mind-Dao shining without corner or remainder. Partial understandings, dualistic good/evil fights, and fragmented rites are incomplete until re-centered in perfect brightness that includes and dissolves obstruction without residue.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Lingbao claims a universal, luminous soteriology. 2) Premise: luminosity that is not round still leaves dark sectors of self and world. 3) Inference: practice must aim at completeness of illumination, not trophy techniques. 4) Inference: when 圆明 is realized, disasters and confusions lose ontological density. 5) Conclusion: the great meaning is perfect bright wholeness as both doctrine and method.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Audit BaZi remedies for partiality—boosting wealth while ignoring health/ethics is non-round. 2) Meditate a full-sphere light encompassing all ten directions of the chart’s problems. 3) Convert dualistic 'kill the evil star' talk into illumination-and-integration strategy where possible. 4) Use confession to clear the dark sector that blocks roundness. 5) End each session asking: what corner of life remains unilluminated?
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 自然经诀’s emphasis on spontaneity of method, this names perfect luminosity as the doctrinal core. Unlike 升玄消灾’s practical short ascent for protection, it articulates a full Lingbao philosophical soteriology of 圆明. The difference is completeness of meaning versus either methodological ziran or emergency ascent.

entries.name_han: 老子微旨例略
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Laozi’s intent is captured by subtle essentials illustrated through brief examples (微旨例略), not by multiplying words or reifying the Dao as a being among beings. Governing self and world succeeds through emptiness, non-coercive action, and return to the root; verbose systems that clutch forms miss the pivot the text isolates.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Dao that can be fully objectified in speech is already secondary. 2) Premise: Wang Bi-style exegesis shows that brief, well-chosen examples open the subtle hinge. 3) Inference: political and personal order arise from holding the empty center (无). 4) Inference: coercive accumulation of techniques increases disorder. 5) Conclusion: the true 'example' of the Dao is minimal, root-holding action that lets the many self-order.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi counseling, state the one useful-god sentence before the encyclopedia of gods. 2) Prefer subtraction (remove draining habits/relations) over adding more charms. 3) When a day-master is weak, 'hold the center' with rest and resource, not constant fighting. 4) Use silence and empty-mind sits as direct training in 微旨. 5) Test advice by whether it reduces friction in the client’s system.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike revealed thunder, dipper, and talisman scriptures that expand celestial bureaucracy, this contracts discourse to subtle philosophical hinge. Unlike Benji jing’s elaborate origin-liberation metaphysics with Buddhist dialogue, it remains classical Laozi-Wang Bi minimalism. The difference is method: example-brief subtlety versus revealed pantheon or emptiness scholasticism.

entries.name_han: 太玄真一本际经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that all beings share a True One ultimate origin/boundary (本际), and that bondage is ignorance of this shared source while liberation is return to it—often framed with a sophistication that absorbs and answers Buddhist-style questions about emptiness, beginning, and salvation. Ritual and ethics help, but the decisive turn is recognizing that the 'edge' of reality is the True One already present, not a foreign place to be manufactured.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: phenomena are secondary to the True One’s ultimate boundary-origin. 2) Premise: sentient error is mistaking derivatives for the root. 3) Inference: doctrines of pure nothingness or pure being both miss 本际 if they block return. 4) Inference: scripture, precepts, and contemplation reorient mind to the shared origin. 5) Conclusion: deliverance is ontological homecoming to the True One’s boundary, not endless management of symptoms.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When BaZi analysis becomes infinite complication, stop and re-center on the single True One of the chart (day-master as local image of 真一). 2) Use origin-contemplation to dissolve identity fused with temporary luck pillars. 3) Treat moral precepts as clearing noise so 本际 can be noticed. 4) In multi-faith clients, translate without forcing: return-to-source language bridges Daoist and empty-nature insights carefully. 5) Evaluate progress as less ontological panic, more root-stability.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 妙始经’s shorter cosmogonic marvel-beginning rhetoric, 本际经 develops a sustained philosophical soteriology of ultimate origin under Tang-era doctrinal pressure. Unlike 老子微旨例略’s brief classical subtlety, it is expansive and dialogical. The difference is historical task: articulate Daoist ultimate reality as 本际 against competing emptiness discourses while keeping salvific return central.

entries.name_han: 太清真人授道经
entries.logic_thesis: It proves that authentic Dao transmission in the Taiqing lineage must be conferred by a Perfected of Great Clarity rank; method without such conferral is incomplete even if texts are possessed. The scripture’s logic is pedagogical and legal: the Dao is a living current passed through qualified beings, so self-appointment cannot substitute for 授道. Alchemy and practice inherit their safety and efficacy from that current.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Taiqing methods refine the person toward Great Clarity. 2) Premise: the Perfected who already abides there can transmit the living measure of the work. 3) Inference: books alone lack the calibrated current and corrections of transmission. 4) Inference: unauthorized practice risks imbalance and false fire. 5) Conclusion: true cultivation begins when the Dao is received, not merely read.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat mentor/lineage stars in BaZi (resource, officer under restraint, noble people) as indicators of transmission timing. 2) Do not escalate internal alchemy intensity without supervision if the chart shows unstable fire/wind. 3) Prepare for reception by ethics, health, and study—merit attracts proper 授. 4) After any transmission, stabilize with months of ordinary discipline before advanced claims. 5) Read 'meeting a master' luck cycles as structural, then act with humility.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Zhengyi 盟威 texts that stress celestial covenant registers for exorcistic office, this stresses Taiqing perfected conferral for the path of clarity/alchemy. Unlike hagiographic anthologies that show many paths after the fact, it normatively requires transmission at the start. The difference is gatekeeping logic: Great Clarity is entered by bestowal from one who is already there.
